findings.text: `pnpm test:e2e -- tests/e2e/report.spec.ts` and the manual smoke 'export the PDF from the Play webview and open the file in Downloads' were not run. They are the capability checks of CAP-dm-report (AC-dm-36 in the browser) and depend on the frontend files src/api/reportApi.ts, src/features/result/ExportReportDialog.tsx, src/features/result/ResultPage.tsx and on tests/e2e/report.spec.ts, none of which belong to this unit. Deferred integration evidence.

The exported PDF was not looked at as a rendered page: the Read tool needs `pdftoppm` (poppler), which is not installed here, and `@napi-rs/canvas` (needed by unpdf to rasterize) is not a dependency. As a substitute, the text positions of a sample report were dumped with pdfjs (unpdf `getDocumentProxy`): 3 pages, nothing past the right margin, section headings kept with their first block; glyph coverage of the four embedded fonts was checked against every character the model and the catalogs can print (fontkit `hasGlyphForCodePoint`, none missing). The look (spacing, bars, colors) still needs a human glance at the file exported in the Play.

`pnpm test -- <files>` runs the whole vitest suite: pnpm forwards the literal `--` and vitest treats it as the end of options, so the file filter is dropped. The unit's Done-when command therefore ran 14 files / 649 tests (all passed, exit 0). The two unit files alone also pass (`pnpm exec vitest run tests/unit/reportModel.test.ts tests/api/reportRoutes.test.ts`: 49 tests, exit 0).

The embedded fonts are the `latin` subset of @fontsource (Latin-1 plus general punctuation), which covers every fixed text of the report and Portuguese company names. A company name with characters outside it (Greek, Cyrillic, CJK, emoji, Latin Extended such as 'ł') prints as a missing-glyph box in the PDF; the file name is not affected (it keeps those characters, only unsafe ones are replaced). Widening it means embedding the `latin-ext` files too; not done because the owner's context is Brazilian Portuguese.

`@types/pdfkit` types the `font` option of `new PDFDocument` as `string`, while pdfkit also accepts a Buffer. The renderer passes `font: ""` (pdfkit then loads no default font) and registers the four embedded fonts by name, so the file never references Helvetica; the API test asserts there is no Helvetica/Times/Courier in the PDF bytes.

`defaultDownloadsDir()` in server/files/downloadsFolder.ts (`<home>/Downloads`) has no caller yet: server/main.ts, which is not in this unit's files, still builds the same path inline with `path.join(os.homedir(), "Downloads")`. Both give the same folder; phase 4 (backup) or the integration owner may switch main.ts to the helper. The folder is created on the first save when missing (tested).

tests/api/reportRoutes.test.ts reads the saved PDF back with unpdf and finds company, date, calculation version, confidence, stage, lock, the 8 dimension names with their scores, the risks with probability/impact, the 3 actions in order and the guidance notice; the saved name is {company}-{date}.pdf; hostile names (../, ..\, CON, nul, :*?"<>|, ???, .., hidden) stay inside the folder; a draft answers 409 diagnosis_not_completed; an unwritable folder answers 500 write_failed with no file left and the diagnosis unchanged. The 'cancel' branch of the AC does not exist server-side: the plan saves straight to Downloads, so the server never sees a cancel.
Forbidden-term scan (V1-V4, Método V4, V4 Company, PPA, CREP, vacinas) over the report model strings (3 diagnoses) and over the text extracted from two real PDFs (stage 1 and stage 4): no hit.

messages.text: IF-006 is live: POST /api/diagnoses/:id/report (no body; send Content-Type: application/json like every write) answers 200 { fileName, directory } with the name actually used (a name already taken gets ' (2)', ' (3)', so fileName can differ from {company}-{date}.pdf). Errors use the shared shape { error: { code, message } }: 404 diagnosis_not_found, 409 diagnosis_not_completed (draft), 500 write_failed (the message is already user-facing pt-BR and says the result stays open and nothing changed). Any other failure is the generic 500 internal_error. An archived completed diagnosis can be exported. There is no save dialog and no 'cancel' on the server: the frontend shows the failure in role="alert" and leaves the result as it is.

For src/api/reportApi.ts and ExportReportDialog.tsx: show `directory` and `fileName` from the response as the place the file was saved. The folder is the one `createApp` receives as `downloadsDir` (server/main.ts: <home>/Downloads). The date in the name is the diagnosis' completion day in the machine's local time zone, formatted yyyy-mm-dd.

Checks left for the integration owner: (1) `pnpm test:e2e -- tests/e2e/report.spec.ts` once the frontend files and the spec exist (the e2e Downloads folder must be a temporary one passed as `downloadsDir`); (2) in the Play dev-link, conclude a diagnosis, click 'Exportar PDF', open the file in Downloads and glance at the layout (3 pages for a typical stage 1 result: header and 4 facts, stage and lock, 3 actions and the guidance box, 8 dimension bars, numbers, risks, confidence note, footer 'Página x de y'); (3) the full `pnpm test` and `pnpm test:e2e` suites.

server/files/downloadsFolder.ts is reusable for the backup export: `saveFile({ directory, stem, extension, content })` sanitizes the stem (max 80 chars, no separators or reserved characters, Windows device names prefixed with '_'), creates the folder if missing, writes to a '.<uuid>.tmp' file in the same folder, reserves the final name with an exclusive create (' (2)' suffix when taken) and renames; any failure removes the temporary file and the reserved name and throws `FileWriteError` (map it to DomainError 500 write_failed as reportService does).
